one_sentence_story: In April 1861, Paul Broca showed that Louis Victor Leborgne ('Patient Tan') kept sharp comprehension and finger-counting while losing speech to a left inferior frontal lesion — founding cortical localization and left-hemisphere dominance, later deepened when Nina Dronkers MRI-scanned Tan's preserved brain in 2007.
so_what_for_you: When communicating with someone recovering from expressive aphasia after a stroke, speak with normal adult respect, give unhurried time, and welcome gestures, writing, or singing (which recruits intact right-hemisphere melody circuits!).
